transcript.text: Good morning, both of you. Thank you for making time. As you know, we have a proposal to convert the unused paved courtyard into a science learning garden, with planting of six species in the existing soil starting in September and three science lessons held there. Before I make my final approval decision, I need each of you to report anything you think should be included or addressed in the plan. Let's start with you — what concerns or additions do you see that we need to factor in before we finalize?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. Yesterday I received a soil laboratory report for the courtyard that found lead at 185 parts per million, which is above our district's 100-ppm threshold. District procedure requires us to remove the top 8 inches of soil and replace it with certified clean soil before students can use the garden. This report is still in my facilities folder awaiting weekly review and hasn't been added to the project proposal yet. This needs to be factored into the plan and budget before any approval decision is made.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise an important issue as well. This week I received the finalized terms of the science department's garden-learning grant, which was awarded after the proposal was drafted. The grant requires the project to include exactly 10 native plant species — not 6 as currently proposed. It also requires exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026 — not 3. And it requires supervised maintenance to be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. The current proposal doesn't meet any of these requirements, and we need to revise it to comply with the grant terms before approval.
